a-t-i-c.text: To provide the University technologies, informations, services and products to the farmers through single window system, ATIC was established under the name of Kisan Seva Kendra at Gate No. 4 of this University. Apart from this, toll free helpline Agricultural Service is also provided to the farmers on toll free number 18001803001 on Monday, Tuesday and Friday from 10.00 to 12.00. In addition to this toll free helpline Agricultural Service is rendered from KVK Bawal on phone No. 18001804002 on the above said date and time and from Regional Research Station of CCS HAU, Hisa, Uchani, toll free helpline service is provided on phone No. 18001803111 on Monday and Thursday from 10 to 11 A.M.

about-e-e-i-1.title: About EEI
about-e-e-i-1.text: The Department of Agriculture and Cooperation, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmer’s Welfare, Govt. of India has established four EEIs for four regions of the country: EEI (Northern Region) at Nilokheri, Haryana (1959), EEI (Southern Region) at Hyderabad, Andhra Pradesh (1962), EEI (Western Region) at Anand, Gujarat (1962), and EEI (NE Region) at Jorhat, Assam (1987). The Extension Education Institute, Nilokheri was established in 1959 as the first training institute of its kind in the country during the second five-year plan period. The institute’s main mandate is to provide in-service training to middle-level extension functionaries. It is one of the pioneer and premier extension training institutes of the country which carries the responsibility of organizing training courses for the various departments including Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry & Dairy, Forestry, Fisheries, Sericulture, Watershed Management, Rural Development, and Master Trainers of SAMETIs of the northern states of India viz. Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Union Territories of J&K, Ladakh and Chandigarh. In the year 1991, its administrative control was handed over to CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar and since then it functions under the administrative control of CCS HAU, Hisar on the basis of a Memorandum of Understanding between DAC, MoA, GOI, New Delhi, and EEI, Nilokheri.

achievements.title: Achievements
achievements.text: Sale of seeds, non-seed items, planting materials, university publications and all other products of the university are sold to the farmers and other interested persons through a Single Window delivery system. Farm Advisory Services are provided to the farmers and other growers through: a) Personal contacts to the visiting farmers b) Toll Free telephone helpline c) Publication materials and d) Lecturers delivered during various trainings and visiting groups at the centre.

aims-and-objectives.title: Aims and objectives
aims-and-objectives.text: To provide in-service training to the staff of the State Training Institute / Regional Institutes of Rural Development in Extension Teaching Methods and Communication Media. To organize workshops on Communication & Extension Teaching Methods / Training Methodology for Master Trainers / Sub-Divisional Agricultural Officers / Subject Matter Specialists working under broad based Agricultural Extension System. To conduct workshops in specialized fields like Monitoring and Evaluation, Human Resource Development, Entrepreneurship, market Led Extension & Extension for Personnel working under broad based Agricultural Extension System. To undertake programme of publication and production of basic teaching / training material as relevant to extension personnel. To have continuous programme of field studies on Extension Education and allied subjects.

dee-agricultural-technology-information-.title: Agricultural Technology Information Centre
dee-agricultural-technology-information-.text: Knowledge and information are the most essential inputs of the era and must be effectively communicated to the farmers to respond successfully to the opportunities & challenges of social economic & technological changes for the improvement of agricultural productivity, food security & rural livelihoods. Agricultural Technology Information Centre (ATIC) popularly known as ‘Kisan Seva Kendra'came into existence at CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar in February, 2002. ATIC is situated near Gate No. 4 of CCS HAU, Hisar which is easily approachable to the farmers for taking the inputs in form of crop seeds, vegetable seeds, university literature and advisory services. Farm advisory services are provided to the farmers and other growers through Tollfree Helpline Number (18001803001 on Monday, Wednesday & Friday from 10:00am to 1:00pm). Recently Virtual Krishi Samasaya Samadhan Seva has also been started on the day of Toll free helpline through google meet link : ftf-bkqu- mae. Farmers can interact with resource person through this link, by showing live samples of their field problems (insect-pests, disease and other problems etc.).

dee-directorate.title: Directorate
dee-directorate.text: At its inception, Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar "conceived and implemented a unique system of extension education for the transfer of its technology to the farming community". "This set up has been highly commended by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) Review Committee (1978) under the chairmanship of late Dr. M.S. Randhawa" and was admired at the national level. The Directorate of Extension Education acts as a bridge between the researchers and the farming community and the other beneficiaries to provide feedback. Therefore, the role of Directorate of Extension Education is in two ways i.e. , transfer of technologies from scientists to the farming community through field functionaries and to find out the troubles of the field to be passed on to various research departments for finding their solutions. ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE OF DIRECTORATE The Directorate of Extension Education is works under the supervision of Director, who is assisted by Associate Director (Farm Advisory Services); Associate Director (SNIATTE); Manager (ATIC); Associate Director (Publications); Joint Director (Farm Information and Communication Services); Regional Director (EEI, Nilokheri, Karnal) and Senior Coordinator/Coordinator (Krishi Vigyan Kendras). The decisions regarding policies and future plan related to extension programmes are taken by the Extension Education Advisory Committee which is a statutory body The Directorate has a statutory role to play with regard to extension. Extension service is a vehicle, which carries scientific agricultural technology interventions developed of the Research Stations/ Departments to the farm for the overall benefit of the farming community. This noble activity facilities in bridging the identified technological gaps existing with the farmers. The ultimate goal of this important function of the university is to enhance the sustainable net income of the farmer by taking all the enterprises on the farm into consideration, integrating them and treating the whole farm as one unit. This major function of extension is accomplished through dissemination of farm information, training of farmers and extension functionaries, educating the farmers through field activities such as demonstrations, field visits, field days and farm advisory services etc.

dee-saina-nehwal-institute-of-agricultur.title: Saina Nehwal Institute of Agricultural Technology, Training & Education
dee-saina-nehwal-institute-of-agricultur.text: Extension education is one of the three major functions of the CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar. The responsibility for planning, organizing, conducting and coordinating the extension education activities of the university in the Haryana State lies with the Directorate of Extension Education. Its main aim is to transfer the well proven/tested technology to the farmers (males and females), livestock owners, rural youth, field staff of State Govt. and other personnel engaged in developmental and professional agencies in the sphere of agriculture, animal husbandry, horticulture, home agencies and other allied areas through its well planned, skill-oriented and need based programmes. An excellent collaboration/linkage is maintained with the Haryana State Govt. Department of Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry, Social Welfare (Woman and Child Development) etc. and non-government organization so that technologies may reach to the beneficiaries at their door steps. This institute came into existence as Junior Staff School after bifurcation of the University, though trainings have been started in 1965. In 1973, the school was renamed as Institute of Agricultural Technology, Training and Education and in 2013. It was further renamed as Saina Nehwal Institute of Agricultural Technology, Training and Education. This institute disseminate the latest technical know how through various training programmes to farming community and field extension personnel like officers of State Agriculture Department, Semi – Govt. and co-operative organizations like IFFCO, KRIBHCCO, and probationers/Asst. Commissioners (under training) HCS Probationers (under training) etc.

directorate-of-extension-education.title: Directorate of Extension Education
directorate-of-extension-education.text: Extension education is one of the three major functions of the CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar. The responsibility for planning, organizing, conducting and coordinating the extension education activities of the university in the Haryana State lies with the Directorate of Extension Education. Its main aim is to transfer the well proven/tested technology to the farmers (males and females), livestock owners, rural youth, field staff of State Govt. and other personnel engaged in developmental and professional agencies in the sphere of agriculture, animal husbandry, horticulture, home agencies and other allied areas through its well planned, skill-oriented and need based programmes. An excellent collaboration/linkage is maintained with the Haryana State Govt. Department of Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry, Social Welfare (Woman and Child Development) etc. and non-government organization so that technologies may reach to the beneficiaries at their door steps. The approach undertaken is educational with major emphasis on whole farm and family development. Since its inception, the university has conceived and implemented a unique system of extension education for transfer of technology to its ultimate users. The Directorate acts as bridge between the research scientist and the farmers and other beneficiaries to provide feed back, therefore, the role of the Directorate is two fold, i.e., transfer of technologies from scientists to the ultimate clients through field functionaries and to find out the field problems to be passed on to various research departments for working on a solution to the problem.

extension-activities-14.title: Extension Activities
extension-activities-14.text: Extension Activities The Institute organizes training and workshops for middle-level extension personnel including Subject Matter Specialists, Sub Divisional Agricultural Officers, Agriculture Development Officers, Horticulture development officers and other in-service professionals working in the Department of Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry, Social forestry, Fisheries, Sericulture etc. of the eight northern states viz. Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Uttrakhand, Delhi, Bihar, Jharkhand and three union territories i.e. Jammu & Kashmir, Laddakh and Chandigarh. Along with these training programmes EEI, Nilokheri also conducts workshops for the Extension Professionals, Scientists and Master Trainers working in Agricultural Universities and Krishi Vigyan Kendras of above mentioned states. farmers-first-scheme.title: Farmers First Scheme
farmers-first-scheme.text: Farmers FIRST Scheme The Farmers FIRST (Farmer’s Farm, Innovations, Resources, Science and Technology programme as a concept of ICAR is developed as farmer in a centric role for research problem identification, prioritization and conduct of experiments and its management at farmers’ conditions. The focus is on Farmer’s Farm, Innovations, Resources, Science and Technology (FIRST). Integrated agriculture development is based more on efficient resource management. Keeping this in view, 124 the present project is being implemented to give desired focus to the farmers’ needs, resources and local environment. The farmers will be treated as an active partner in the development and transfer of technologies for both decision making and implementation. The overall objective of the project is to use the research information in such a way that it matches well with the on-farm situations. Gurana village has been selected which is free from urbanization with minimum absentee landlords. The information about the agro-eco-systems and socio-economic conditions of this village has been obtained through suitable Participatory Rural Appraisal Techniques (PRA). A total of 1000 farm families have been benefitted through this project of two years duration. The soil conditions, cropping patterns, preferences to crops and requirements have been assessed. The common problems of the Gurana village have been prioritized with farmer’s participation considering their needs and resources. Hence, different technology modules encompassing areas of integrated farming has been formulated in consultation with the farmers. A participatory planning exercise involving the farmers provides basis for these modules. The modules include introduction of crops, pest and weed management practices, livestock management and activities for income augmentation to meet the needs of the farmers considering their problems, resources and willingness to act upon Farmers First Scheme Legacy document 1688704467.pdf — pending Phase 4 upload ( legacy-pending/cms/1932/1688704467.pdf ).

mous-between-ccshau-hisar-and-asci-cirb.title: MoUs between CCSHAU, Hisar and ASCI & CIRB
mous-between-ccshau-hisar-and-asci-cirb.text: MoU between CCSHAU, Hisar and Agriculture Skill Council of India (ASCI) The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was made on 6 th day of December, 2016 between CCSHAU, Hisar and Agriculture Skill Council of India. Saina Nehwal Institute of Agricultural Technology, Training & Education of Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University has been made a training centre and training partner of Agriculture Skill Council of India (ASCI). The Centre SNIATTE has been registered by ASCI SDMS Reg. No NSDC-REG No. 16670 and has been allotted as training centre ID 107787 to award Certificate/Diploma of skill development in 16 different disciplines. One training for Master Trainers’ has been organized from January 03-05, 2018. Twenty scientists from various disciplines from College of Agriculture and Agricultural Engineering have been certified as “Master Trainers”. The course content being followed for various job roles was further improved and supplemented under various sub-heads of the topic by the Master Trainers of CCSHAU, Hisar from various departments of COA & COAE & T on the pattern of ASCI was approved in the 479 th (Emergent) meeting of The Academic Council, CCSHAU, Hisar held on 27.10.2018 and approved vide No. Acad./18/A-1/ACP/35927-49 dated 6.11.18. MoU between CCSHAU, Hisar and Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes (CIRB) MoU was made on 10.10.2019 between Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar as first party and ICAR-Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes, Hisar as an second party for organization of skill trainings under SCSP prpgramme for the farmers/members of SC community. Wherein, the CCSHAU, Hisar will conduct these trainings ICAR-CIRB would meet out all expenses going to be incurred in organizing these trainings. The SINATTE, Director of Extension Education, CCSHAU, Hisar shall provide all the facilities including (faculty and infrastructure) for conductance of theses trainings.

physical-facilities.title: Physical Facilities
physical-facilities.text: University Exhibition University level exhibition has been established & maintained by this Unit under the umbrella of Directorate of Extension Education. It was inaugurated on February 02, 1994 by Honorable Governor of Haryana Sh. Dhanik Lal Mandal. This exhibition is frequently visited by persons from all ranks and files. In fact, this exhibition is a show window of the techniques/ technologies evolved/ developed by the different departments of the university in a comprehensive and effective manner. Almost daily it is being visited by the scientists, students, defense personnel, farmers, etc. not only from the state of Haryana but other states of Indian Union too. Haryana Rural Antique Museum There is no denying fact that Haryana has got a rich cultural heritage. To highlight this unique cultural heritage of Haryana, Haryana Rural Antique Museum was established in Gandhi Bhawan by Dr J.C. Sharma, first Director of Extension Education. It is maintained by this Unit under the umbrella of Directorate of Extension Education. Formally this museum was inaugurated on February 02, 1989 by Dr Har Sawroop Singh then worthy Vice chancellor, HAU, Hisar. This Museum not only highlights cultural details but also provides linkages between the old and new culture. The museum being a part of the Directorate of Extension Education of an Agricultural University, it was considered appropriate to preserve and display all those things related with agriculture in particular and rural life in general. Up gradation and modernization work of this museum is in process. In brief, the old agricultural implements, costumes, household items, pottery pieces and the art objects have been displayed in an artistic manner so as to attract and educate the visitors about the rich culture of Haryana. Several new editions have been added to the existing collections.

scientific-advisory-committee-meeting.title: Scientific Advisory Committee Meeting
scientific-advisory-committee-meeting.text: Scientific Advisory Committee Meeting The Scientific Advisory Committee Meeting is a regular feature and being conducted at concerned KVKs once a year during the month of September/October every year at all the ICAR funded KVKs under the Chairmanship of Vice-Chancellor. In the absence of Vice-Chancellor, Director of Extension Education is the Chairman of SAC meetings. In these meetings, Senior Coordinator/Coordinator presents the salient findings and achievements of KVK particularly of various OFTs and FLDs which they conducted during both the seasons. They also present the action plan for the coming year. Progressive farmers also attend such meetings to express their views and expectations from the KVK. This is a useful platform to have interactive meeting of scientists, farmers and field staff of Deptt. of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare, Govt. of Haryana and scientists from the line departments so as to take the benefit of collective wisdom for the benefits of farming community of Haryana.

trainings-2.title: Trainings
trainings-2.text: Training Our agenda is simple: “We work to improve and strengthen the practice of vocational education and training” The belief that skills are key to achieve economic and social propriety underpins all of our work. Agriculture skill will continue to hold the key to reduce poverty and unrising the security of livelihoods in many developing countries. The major challenges in terms of potential conflicts over increasing food and water security and the unpredictable long terms of effects of climate change continue to rant.Small farmers, NGOs, GO’s and policy makers in developing countries are all grapping with these challenges at different levels. To deal with these issues the importance of training cannot be underestimated. The skills to improve productivity, increase adaptability to deal with change and crises and facilitate the diversification of livelihood to manage risks are at a premium in rural areas. Training is a process acquisition of new skills attitudes and knowledge in the context of preparing for entry into a vocation or improving ones productivity in an organization or enterprise. Further training is directed towards improving the efficiency in farming activities that begins with need identification and after a number of steps ends with evaluation of the training actively. Designing a training and development programme involved a sequence of steps that can be grouped into five phases; need assessment, objections, design, implementation and evaluation. In India, like other nations, the production practices and skills are passed from generation to generation. This informal apprenticeship has worked well, however, there is strange need to build on this mentoring tradition. This is where the programme for skill development became important.It is common to find the rural India several common agricultural practices being followed wrongly. Now, are becoming aware about how to do things better. We now understand that skill development aims at equipping us with skill sets to successfully and sustainably perform activities. Another important dimension of skilling is that it is not a one time activity or process. Reskilling and upgration of skill is a continuous process. Skill India is an initiative of the Government of India which has been launched to empower the youth of the country with skill sets which make them more employable and more productive in their work environment. Our National Skill Mission is chaired by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi himself. India is a country today with 65% of its youth in working age group. If ever there a way to reap this demographic advantage, it has to be through skill development of the youth so that they add not only to their personal growth, but to the country’s economic growth as well.
